subject: National Values Education
examFormat: National Values Education (NVE) combines Civic Education, Security Education and Social Studies. Civic Education: National Values Education (NVE) is a fusion of Civic Education, Security Education and Social Studies; it assesses the development of Nigerian youth as responsible citizens, their moral, social, political and intellectual knowledge in nation-building, their ability to recognise the dimensions of human beings in different cultural and social contexts, and their level of security consciousness. Civic Education is examined in Paper 1 of BECE National Values Education, which has sixty multiple-choice questions: 50 from Civic Education and 10 from Security Education. (Social Studies is examined separately in Paper 2.) Security Education: National Values Education (NVE) is a fusion of Civic Education, Security Education and Social Studies; it assesses the development of Nigerian youth as responsible citizens, their moral, social, political and intellectual knowledge in nation-building, their ability to recognise the dimensions of human beings in different cultural and social contexts, and their level of security consciousness. Security Education is examined in Paper 1 of BECE National Values Education, which has sixty multiple-choice questions: 10 from Security Education and 50 from Civic Education. Social Studies: National Values Education (NVE) is a fusion of Civic Education, Security Education and Social Studies; it assesses the development of Nigerian youth as responsible citizens, their moral, social, political and intellectual knowledge in nation-building, their ability to recognise the dimensions of human beings in different cultural and social contexts, and their level of security consciousness. Social Studies is examined in Paper 2 of BECE National Values Education, which has sixty multiple-choice questions on Social Studies.
excluded: Built from the component subjects; see each component.

topics.name: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
objectives: Explain the meaning, levels of manifestation and importance of values in the society
Explain the meaning, attributes and benefits of honesty and the consequences of dishonesty
Explain the meaning, attributes, promoting factors and benefits of cooperation
Explain the meaning, attributes and benefits of self-reliance
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Our Values. Covers values, honesty, cooperation and self-reliance as national values.

subtopics.name: Values
objectives: Explain the meaning of values: likes and dislikes
Identify the levels of manifestation of values: individual and society
State the importance of values in the society: unity, cooperation and harmony
Identify factors that promote a value system: consistency, trust, tolerance, fairness, integrity and commitment

subtopics.name: Honesty
objectives: Explain the meaning of honesty
List the attributes of honesty
State the benefits of honesty
Explain the consequences of dishonesty, e.g. in examination malpractice, cheating and fraudulent practices

subtopics.name: Cooperation
objectives: Explain the meaning of cooperation
List the attributes of cooperation: sharing, caring, supporting etc.
Identify factors that promote cooperation
State the benefits of cooperation: harmony, progress and goal achievement

subtopics.name: Self-Reliance
objectives: Explain the meaning of self-reliance
List the attributes of self-reliance
Describe the processes of identifying, nurturing and perfecting talents and skills
State the benefits of self-reliance to oneself, the family and the society
Understand that the wealth of a nation is contained in its natural and human resources
Explain the consequences of undiscovered talents and undeveloped skills

topics.name: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
objectives: Explain the meaning and attributes of integrity, contentment, discipline and courage
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Our Values. The syllabus heading names integrity, contentment and discipline; courage is listed under the same topic.

subtopics.name: Integrity
objectives: Explain the meaning of integrity
List the attributes of integrity: probity and honesty, contentment, truthfulness, fair-play and non-compromise of principles
Give examples of people of integrity in the society
Explain the need for people of integrity in the society

subtopics.name: Contentment
objectives: Explain the meaning of contentment
List the attributes of contentment: satisfaction, lack of envy, rejection of greed and corruption, humility etc.
Explain the effects of lack of contentment on the society: corruption, greed, envy, prostitution, robbery, cheating etc.

subtopics.name: Discipline
objectives: Explain the meaning of discipline
List the attributes of discipline: self-control, moderation, modesty, respect for legitimate authority, respect for rules and regulations, perseverance, dedication etc.

subtopics.name: Courage
objectives: Explain the meaning of courage
Identify the types of courage: physical, moral and spiritual
List the attributes of a courageous person: commitment, endurance, determination, steadfastness, diligence, boldness, bravery etc.

topics.name: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
objectives: Explain the meaning of right attitude to work
List the attributes of right attitude to work: honesty, discipline, integrity, commitment, punctuality, regularity, consistency, diligence, transparency etc.
State the importance of reward: higher productivity, efficiency, progress, recognition and improved national image
Explain the consequences of not having the right attitude to work: declining productivity, lack of motivation, indiscipline and national disasters (air, sea, road etc.)
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Our Values.

topics.name: Negative Behaviour
objectives: Explain the meaning of negative behaviour
Identify types of negative behaviour: dishonesty, excessive love of money, ostentatious living, disregard for time, drug trafficking, examination malpractice, cultism etc.
Explain the effects of negative behaviour: value disorientation, inefficiency, high crime rate etc.
Suggest ways of promoting positive behaviour
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Our Values.

topics.name: Citizenship
objectives: Explain the meaning of citizenship
Identify the types of citizenship: by birth, by registration and by naturalisation
Describe the process of becoming a citizen of a country
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Citizenship.

topics.name: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
objectives: Explain the meaning of rights and duties
Differentiate between rights and duties
State the importance of citizens' rights and duties: social control, peace, due process and discipline
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Citizenship.

topics.name: Supremacy of the Constitution
objectives: Explain the supremacy of the constitution
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Citizenship.

topics.name: The Constitution
objectives: Explain the meaning of constitution
Identify the constitutions of colonial Nigeria: Clifford Constitution 1922, Richards Constitution 1946, Macpherson Constitution 1951, Lyttelton Constitution 1954 and Independence Constitution 1960
State the features of the colonial constitutions
Identify the post-1960 constitutions: 1963, 1979 and 1989 Constitutions
State the features of the post-1960 constitutions
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Citizenship.

topics.name: Objects for National Consciousness
objectives: Identify the national symbols: coat of arms, national flag and national currency
Recite and explain the National Anthem and Pledge
State the purpose of establishing national institutions like the NYSC, Unity Schools and Federal Character
Suggest ways of promoting national unity: tolerance, hospitality, non-discrimination, inter-marriage etc.
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: National Consciousness and Identity.

topics.name: Nigeria as a Federation
objectives: Explain the meaning of federation
State the need for federation: national integration, unity in diversity and controlling activities of states

Describe the characteristics of a federation: sharing of powers between central and state governments; states have constitutionally defined control over their own affairs; central government controls the states; constitution of the federation
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Governance.

topics.name: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
objectives: Describe the relationship between the tiers of government: performing functions according to constitutional provisions, power to legislate, and power to carry out functions in accordance with constitutional provisions
Differentiate among the three tiers of government in functions, legislative powers, executive powers, and concurrent and exclusive powers
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Governance.

topics.name: The Rule of Law
objectives: Explain the meaning of law and rule of law
State the benefits of rule of law as against arbitrary rule
Explain punishment for breaking the law
Explain the equality of all citizens before the law
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Human Rights and the Rule of Law.

topics.name: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
objectives: Describe ways of protecting human rights: representing the affected persons in court; drawing attention to cases of human rights violations through protest marches, media coverage and hunger strikes
Identify groups that assist in protecting the human rights of citizens: civil society organisations (e.g. CLO, CDHR, CRP), trade unions, students unions, ethnic associations and the Legal Aid Council
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Human Rights and the Rule of Law.

topics.name: Consumer Rights and Responsibilities
objectives: State the universal rights of a consumer: satisfaction of basic needs, safety, information, redress, consumer education, representation (to be heard) and a healthy environment
State the responsibilities of a consumer: be aware, demand and keep proofs of transactions (receipts, invoices, warranties etc.), think independently, speak out and respect the environment
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Human Rights and the Rule of Law.

topics.name: Democracy
objectives: Explain the meaning of democracy
State the features of democracy
Identify democratic institutions and their functions: INEC, political parties, pressure groups and arms of government
State the importance of democracy
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Democracy.

topics.name: Pillars of Democracy
objectives: Explain the meaning of pillars of democracy
Identify the pillars of democracy: the people, democratic institutions, rule of law, transparent electoral process, majority rule and minority rights etc.
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Democracy.

topics.name: Election and Voter Responsibilities
objectives: Explain the concepts of election, voter and voting
Differentiate between various types of elections
Enumerate the basic qualifications for election
Discuss the responsibilities of a voter
Describe the procedure for voting and discuss the importance of election
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Democracy.

topics.name: Electoral Malpractices
objectives: Explain the meaning of electoral malpractice

Identify forms of electoral malpractice: fake ballot papers, manipulation of votes and multiple voting; artificial scarcity of electoral materials; underage voting; thuggery and intimidation; inducement and corruption; fake manifestoes
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Democracy.

topics.name: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
objectives: Explain the meaning and importance of elections
Identify the electoral bodies: INEC and SIEC for national and state government respectively
Explain the need for free and fair elections
Identify electoral malpractices in Nigeria and how to prevent them
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Democracy.

topics.name: Democratic Voting
objectives: Explain the meaning of voting
Describe voters registration
State the importance of voting
Describe the process of voting
topics.content: Part of Civic Education. Sub-theme: Democracy. (The topic heading is cut off in the source text after "Democratic"; its content is about voting.)

topics.name: Common Crimes, Causes and Effects
objectives: Give examples of crime: falsehood, theft, rape, murder, advance fee fraud (419), sale of contaminated food, dealing in fake drugs etc.
Explain the causes and effects of common crimes
Describe crime prevention through cooperation with security agents, schools and neighbourhood authorities
topics.content: Part of Security Education. Sub-theme: Common Crimes and Security Management.

topics.name: Observing and Reporting Common Crimes
objectives: Describe different ways of observing and reporting common crimes
Demonstrate appropriate response
topics.content: Part of Security Education. Sub-theme: Common Crimes and Security Management.

topics.name: Common Crimes and Associated Punishments
objectives: Match common crimes with their associated punishments: theft (imprisonment), rape (imprisonment), drug trafficking (10 years imprisonment), human trafficking (5–10 years imprisonment), murder (death)
Explain food contamination
Explain drug contamination/adulteration
topics.content: Part of Security Education. Sub-theme: Common Crimes and Security Management.

topics.name: Emergency Management
objectives: Explain the meaning of emergency management
Identify types of emergencies to be managed: accidents, fire, drowning, building collapse, food poisoning etc.
Describe the appropriate response in emergency management
topics.content: Part of Security Education. Sub-theme: Common Crimes and Security Management. (The last listed type of emergency is cut off in the source after "Fake".)

topics.name: Crimes and National Security
objectives: Explain the meaning of national security
Identify crimes that affect national security: pipeline vandalisation, drug trafficking, human trafficking, illegal bunkering, terrorism, arson, importation of expired foods, drugs etc.
Demonstrate awareness of crimes that affect national security
topics.content: Part of Security Education. Sub-theme: Common Crimes and Security Management.

topics.name: History of Nigerian Social Studies Education
objectives: Trace the history of Nigerian Social Studies education
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Fundamentals of Social Studies Education.

topics.name: General Objectives of Social Studies
objectives: State the general objectives of Social Studies
Develop the ability to adapt to a changing environment
Inculcate national consciousness and national unity
Become a good citizen capable of and willing to contribute to the development of the society
Inculcate the right types of values and attitudes
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Fundamentals of Social Studies Education.

topics.name: Contents of Social Studies
objectives: Explain the meaning of Social Studies contents: facts, conceptualisation, skills, values and attitudes relevant for learners and society
Identify the cognitive, affective and psychomotor contents of Social Studies
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Fundamentals of Social Studies Education.

topics.name: Family as a Primary Group
objectives: Explain the meaning of a primary social group
Explain what makes the family a primary group
Describe the roles and responsibilities of members of a social group
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Family as the Basic Unit of the Society.

topics.name: Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes
objectives: Describe the characteristics of a large family size: father, mother and many children
Describe the characteristics of a small family size: father, mother and very few children
Explain the consequences of family size on the quality of individual lives and on the national economy
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Family as the Basic Unit of the Society.

topics.name: Purpose of Marriage
objectives: Explain the meaning of marriage
State the purposes of marriage: procreation, satisfying economic and social needs, sexual satisfaction, growth in mutual love etc.
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Family as the Basic Unit of the Society.

topics.name: Readiness in Marriage
objectives: State the conditions for marriage: physical fitness, psychological fitness, social stability and financial readiness
Explain the effects of lack of readiness on the marriage relationship: constant fights/instability, divorce, broken homes etc.
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Family as the Basic Unit of the Society.

topics.name: Positive Group Behaviours
objectives: Identify types of group behaviour: mass action, communal labour, joining a protest or march, participating in a fight, acting patriotically
State the benefits of positive group behaviours: companionship, survival and security, affiliation and status, power and control, achievement
Describe the characteristics of different types of group behaviour: destructive (negative) and constructive (positive)
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Family as the Basic Unit of the Society.

topics.name: Human Trafficking
objectives: Explain the meaning of human trafficking
Identify factors responsible for children and women trafficking
Explain the consequences of human trafficking: loss of human resources; life of crime, addiction and sexual violence; weakening of family love and influence etc.
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Family as the Basic Unit of the Society.

topics.name: Preventing Human Trafficking
objectives: Describe preventive measures against human trafficking: awareness campaigns, education, advocacy, legislation etc.
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Family as the Basic Unit of the Society.

topics.name: Harmful Traditional Practices
objectives: Explain the meaning of harmful traditional practices
Give examples of harmful traditional practices: use of children for begging, child labour, female circumcision, early marriage etc.
Explain the consequences of harmful traditional practices: problems at childbirth, exploitation of children, deprivation of schooling etc.
Suggest ways of preventing harmful traditional practices
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Family as the Basic Unit of the Society.

topics.name: Promoting Peaceful Living in Our Society
objectives: Explain the meaning of peace, cordial and friendly living among different groups of people
Identify types of peace: positive peace and negative/uneasy peace
State the importance of peace: lack of violence/conflict, progress and development, happiness and less stress etc.
Describe ways of promoting peace: tolerance, social justice, human rights etc.
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Family as the Basic Unit of the Society.

topics.name: Agents and Processes of Socialization
objectives: Explain the meaning of socialization
Identify agents of socialization: family, school, religious organisations, the press, age grades, peer groups, clubs and societies etc.
State the importance of socialization
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Agents of Socialization.

topics.name: Road Safety Club as an Agent of Socialization
objectives: Describe the structure and processes of forming a Road Safety Club in schools
Explain the roles of the Road Safety Club in the socialization of youths
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Agents of Socialization.

topics.name: Common Social Problems in Nigeria
objectives: Identify contemporary social problems in Nigeria
Explain the causes of contemporary social problems in Nigeria
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Social and Health Issues.

topics.name: Ways of Solving Social Problems in Nigeria
objectives: Explain the effects of social problems
Suggest ways of solving contemporary social problems
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Social and Health Issues.

topics.name: Our Roles in Promoting Safety in Our Community
objectives: Explain the need for safety
Describe safety measures in the home, schools and workplaces
State safety guidelines for pedestrians, cyclists, motorcyclists and motorists
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Social and Health Issues.

topics.name: Dangers of Drug Trafficking
objectives: Explain the meaning of drug trafficking
State reasons for trafficking in drugs: poverty, ignorance, greed etc.
Explain the dangers of drug trafficking: bad image for the country, imprisonment, death penalty in some cases, effect on national security, negative impact on the economy etc.

Describe ways of discouraging drug abuse: choosing good friends, forming drug-free clubs, acquiring coping skills (assertiveness, refusal/resistance skills, problem solving, communication and decision-making skills), constructive use of time (e.g. sports, religious activities)
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Social and Health Issues.

topics.name: Preventing Drug Trafficking
objectives: Explain the meaning of drug trafficking
State reasons for trafficking in drugs: poverty, ignorance, greed etc.
Explain the consequences of drug trafficking: bad image for the country, imprisonment, death penalty in some cases, forfeiture of assets (local and foreign) etc.
Describe the prevention of drug trafficking through education, alleviation of poverty, legislation and the international community
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Social and Health Issues.

topics.name: Meaning and Consequences of Drug Abuse and Harmful Substances
objectives: Explain the meaning of drug/substance abuse
Identify forms of drug abuse
Explain the consequences of drug abuse on the individual, the community, the nation and the international community
topics.content: Part of Social Studies. Sub-theme: Social and Health Issues. (The source numbers this topic VII; there is no topic VI in the sub-theme.)
